name: Skill Builder
blurb: a Claude Code SKILL.md with its name, description and trigger words, plus the folder layout
intro: Builds a SKILL.md (YAML frontmatter with name, description and allowed-tools, then When to use, Steps, Files and Notes) and the folder around it, lints both against the Claude Code and Agent Skills docs as of 2026-09 (marked verify), and scores test messages against the description with a word-overlap heuristic to show whether it would plausibly trigger.

inputs.label: Description
inputs.default: Builds, flashes and verifies STM32 firmware over ST-LINK with OpenOCD, then reads back the reset cause. Use when the user asks to flash, program, burn or upload firmware to a board, or when a flash fails with "init mode failed" or "target not halted". Triggers on: "flash the board", "program the MCU", "st-link", "openocd", "karta yükle", "flash et".
inputs.help: What it does and when to use it, with the phrases users say. Max 1024 characters (verify).

inputs.label: allowed-tools
inputs.help: Comma-separated; Bash(cmd:*) narrows Bash to one command. Empty = none.

inputs.label: When to use
inputs.default:
The user wants new firmware on a connected STM32 board (Nucleo or a custom board on SWD).
A flash or verify step failed and the OpenOCD output needs reading.
Not for: building without a board (run the build preset), or J-Link probes (use the jlink-flash skill).

inputs.label: Steps
inputs.default:
Build the release preset: `cmake --preset release && cmake --build build/release`.
Check that a probe is attached with `st-info --probe`; stop and tell the user if none is listed.
Flash and verify with `scripts/flash.sh build/release/app.elf` (OpenOCD program, verify, reset).
If OpenOCD fails, find the error text in references/openocd-errors.md and apply its fix, at most twice.
Read the reset cause from the serial log and report it with the flash result.
inputs.help: One step per line; numbered for you.

inputs.label: Notes
inputs.default:
Never mass-erase unless the user says so: it wipes the calibration page at 0x0807F800.
Each board's OpenOCD target config is listed in references/boards.md.
Keep the OpenOCD log under /home/emir/flash-logs/ for the bug report.

default.purpose: OpenOCD program + verify + reset for one ELF
board -> OpenOCD interface and target cfg

inputs.label: Trigger tests
inputs.default:
+ flash the new build to the nucleo board
+ şu firmware'i karta yükle
+ openocd says target not halted, can you fix it
+ program the MCU and tell me why it reset
- write a unit test for the ring buffer
- what is the baud rate for USART2 on PA2
inputs.help: One user message per line: + should load the skill, - should not.

inputs.label: Trigger threshold
inputs.help: Heuristic score (0-1) at which a message counts as loading the skill.

usage: Give name (kebab), description (what + when + quoted trigger phrases), allowedTools (comma list, Bash(cmd:*) patterns), scope (project/personal/plugin), whenToUse, steps (one per line), notes, files [{path, purpose}] under scripts/ references/ assets/, tests (lines '+ message' should trigger, '- message' should not) and threshold. Returns texts 'SKILL.md' and 'Create folder (sh)' (mkdir + heredoc), a lint table (name format/length, description length/when-clause/person, open Bash, unknown tools, body length, absolute and backslash paths, files referenced but missing) and a trigger-test table with heuristic scores. Use it to write a new skill or to check why an existing one does not trigger.
sources: Anthropic, Agent Skills overview and best practices (docs.claude.com, read 2026-09): name <=64 chars lowercase/digits/hyphens, no reserved words; description <=1024 chars, third person, what + when; SKILL.md body under 500 lines; references one level deep; forward slashes - verify
Anthropic, Claude Code docs: Skills (locations .claude/skills, ~/.claude/skills, plugin skills; allowed-tools) - read 2026-09, verify
Claude Code permission rule syntax: Tool or Tool(specifier), Bash(cmd:*) prefix match - verify
Trigger score: a word-overlap heuristic written for this tool, not the model's selection
